content:
Andy Robertson has emphasized that strengthening Liverpool's defensive performance will be crucial in supporting new manager Arne Slot as the team aims to mount a serious title challenge during his inaugural campaign at the helm. The Scottish left-back expressed optimism about the early results, noting that the team has managed to keep a clean sheet in both of their opening fixtures this season. However, Robertson acknowledged that a significant challenge lies ahead as Liverpool prepares to travel to Old Trafford to face Manchester United, where the defensive unit will undoubtedly be put under considerably more pressure than they experienced in their previous encounters. The matches against Ipswich and Brentford saw Liverpool successfully prevent any goals from being scored against them, providing Slot with an ideal beginning to his tenure. Looking back at the previous campaign, Liverpool's defensive record was notably inferior compared to their main rivals, having allowed 41 goals throughout the 38-match Premier League season as they finished in third position. This total was significantly higher than what Manchester City, the eventual champions, and Arsenal, who claimed second place, conceded during the same period. City let in seven fewer goals while Arsenal's defense was even more impressive, conceding 12 fewer than Liverpool.

Handle the defensive responsibilities more effectively is what Robertson believes will make the difference this season. The experienced defender reflected on the statistics from the previous campaign, pointing out that even during the period when Liverpool remained competitive in the title race, they were giving up more scoring opportunities to their opponents than both Arsenal and Manchester City were allowing. Robertson expressed his understanding that when a team consistently permits more chances than their rivals, there will inevitably come matches where they pay the price for such vulnerabilities. This is precisely what occurred last season, with Liverpool's defensive shortcomings ultimately contributing to their inability to sustain their title challenge against the top two teams. The defender's comments highlight a clear awareness within the squad about what needs to improve if they are to compete at the highest level under their new manager.

Robertson conveyed his hopes that the team can maintain their current defensive momentum as they progress through the season. After facing Manchester United, the squad will have an international break before resuming their campaign, and the defender expressed his desire to continue limiting opposition teams to minimal chances throughout the remainder of the fixtures. The early signs under Slot's guidance have been encouraging, with the two consecutive clean sheets representing exactly the kind of foundation Robertson believes the team needs to build upon. The defender's statements suggest a collective determination within the Liverpool squad to address the defensive issues that plagued them last season and to provide their new manager with the solid defensive platform necessary to challenge for major honors during his first year in charge of the club.

P.S. Liverpool's defensive improvement under Arne Slot will be closely monitored throughout the season as they seek to close the gap on Manchester City and Arsenal in the Premier League standings.
